basics.title: What is it?
basics.description: The fields below adapt to the type.

display.title: How it appears on a CV
display.description: Title, place and dates in {language}. Switch language at the top.

facts.title: What you did
facts.description: One claim per line, in plain words. CVs and letters can only say what is written here.
facts.placeholder: e.g. Cut average response time from 2 days to 4 hours.
facts.emptyBody: Start with what you’re proudest of: one claim per line, with numbers when you have them. Or use “Tell Naruvi” above and write it freely.
facts.backs: {count, plural, one {Backs # CV line} other {Backs # CV lines}}
facts.asLineHint: Add this fact as a CV line, linked to it
facts.long: Long fact. Splitting it into one claim per line makes it easier to cite.
facts.number: A number makes it stronger: how many, how much, how fast, for whom.

bullets.title: CV lines
bullets.description: The polished sentences a CV may use, shown in {language}. Each one points to the facts behind it.
bullets.emptyBody: Draft them from your facts above, or write your own. Group them by theme (e.g. “Cloud”, “Monitoring”) so a CV can pick the ones that match a job.

skills.title: Skills & keywords
skills.description: Helps match this entry to the right jobs.

guardrails.title: Never say
guardrails.description: Limits for CVs and letters about this entry.

leave.title: Leave with unsaved changes?
leave.body: Your edits to this entry will be lost.

deleteDialog.title: Delete “{title}”?
deleteDialog.body: Its facts and bullets are removed too. Archiving keeps them but excludes the entry from generation.

bullet.label: Label: a heading, not a claim
bullet.notBacked: Not backed by a fact yet
bullet.placeholder: A polished CV line, e.g. Cut response time from 2 days to 4 hours by…
bullet.link: Link the fact that proves this

preview.fill: Fill in the {language} display fields to see this entry as it will appear on a CV.
preview.wavy: Wavy underline: not backed by a fact yet; generation will skip it.
preview.title: On your CV

readiness.steps: {count, plural, one {# step before CVs can use it} other {# steps before CVs can use it}}
readiness.skip: CVs and letters skip it until then

experience.0: What was your role, and at which company or organisation?
experience.1: When did it start and end, and where was it?
experience.2: What did you do day to day?
experience.3: What are you proudest of there? Numbers help: how many, how much, how fast, for whom.
experience.4: Which tools, methods or skills did you use?

education.0: What did you study, and at which school?
education.2: Which subjects, projects or thesis are worth mentioning?
education.3: Any results, honours or responsibilities (student association, tutoring…)?

project.0: What is the project, and who was it for?
project.1: What was your part in it?
project.2: What came out of it? Users, results, numbers, links.
project.3: Which tools or methods did you use?

certification.0: Which certification, and who issued it?
certification.1: When did you get it, and does it expire?
certification.2: What did you have to know or do to get it?

achievement.0: What did you achieve or win?
achievement.2: Why does it matter? Numbers or who recognised it.

entryAssist.translatedBody: {count, plural, one {# bullet translated with the same facts linked.} other {# bullets translated with the same facts linked.}}
entryAssist.waiting: Your notes are waiting in the panel.
entryAssist.invite: Tell me about it in your own words, and I’ll fill the fields and facts.
entryAssist.title: Tell me about it
entryAssist.subtitle: Like you’d tell a friend. I only use what you write.
entryAssist.addedBoth: Added {facts, plural, one {# fact} other {# facts}} and {skills, plural, one {# skill} other {# skills}}
entryAssist.dropped: {count} left out: their numbers weren’t in what you wrote.
entryAssist.notSaved: Nothing is saved until you press Save.
entryAssist.freePlaceholder: e.g. From 2021 to 2024 I ran the night shift at a 40-bed hospital ward in Lyon, trained 6 new nurses and set up the medication double-check that cut errors in half…
entryAssist.helps: Dates, numbers and tools help most
entryAssist.answerPlaceholder: Type or dictate. Skip what doesn’t apply.

experience.0: Don’t present freelance or contract work as a permanent job.
experience.1: Don’t claim to have led a team unless a fact says so.
experience.2: Don’t round numbers up or add results that aren’t listed.

project.0: Don’t present a personal project as paid client work.
project.1: Don’t claim users or results that aren’t in the facts.

education.0: Don’t claim the degree before it was awarded.
education.1: Don’t claim honours or rankings that aren’t listed.

certification.0: Don’t list it as current after it expires.

achievement.0: Don’t claim a higher placement than the one stated.

rules.nda: Don’t name clients, internal systems or confidential numbers.
rules.general: Don’t add results that aren’t in the facts.

entryExtras.nothingNewBody: Your tags and rules already cover the facts.

entryExtras.ndaOff: Turn on if you can’t name clients, systems or numbers.
